question.text: Let $C_{1}$ and $C_{2}$ denote the centres of the circles $x^{2}+y^{2}=4$ and $(x-2)^{2}+y^{2}=1$ respectively and let $P$ and $Q$ be their points of intersection.Then, the areas of $\Delta C_{1} P Q$ and $C_{2} P Q$ are in the ratio

solution.text: $x^{2}+y^{2}=4$ $$ \begin{array}{l} (x-2)^{2}+y^{2}=1 \\ C_{1}=(0,0), C_{2}=(2,0) \end{array} $$ On solving Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get $$ \begin{aligned} x=\frac{7}{4}, y=\pm \frac{\sqrt{15}}{4} \\ C_{1} N=\frac{7}{4}, P Q=\frac{2 \sqrt{15}}{4} &=\frac{\sqrt{15}}{2} \\ \frac{\text { Area }\left(\Delta C_{1} P Q\right)}{\text { Area }\left(\Delta C_{2} P Q\right)}=& \frac{\frac{1}{2} \cdot P Q \cdot C_{1} N}{\frac{1}{2} \cdot P Q \cdot C_{2} N} \\ &=\frac{C_{1} N}{C_{2} N}=\frac{\frac{7}{4}}{2-\frac{7}{4}}=\frac{\frac{7}{4}}{\frac{1}{4}}=7: 1 \end{aligned} $$ Hence, the required option is (c).
